searchDocs.title: Key Features​
searchDocs.content: Familiar: This is literally XML and HTML syntax, but in Luau. You're probably familiar with Roblox's RichText too.Efficient: It can handle numerous tags, nested tags, tag attributes, ...Extendable: You can define any tags in any way you want, and they'll work perfectly fine.Runtime Agnostic: You can run Markua in any Luau runtime. It's just one script.

searchDocs.title: Installation​
searchDocs.content: You can install Markua either via Wally or the .rbxm file in the latest release. For usage outside Roblox, you can copy paste the src/standalone/init.luau script directly into your project.

searchDocs.title: Next Steps​
searchDocs.content: Usage Guide.Roblox Integration.

searchDocs.title: TextObject​
searchDocs.content: </> type TextObject = TextLabel | TextBox | TextButton

searchDocs.title: TextFormatter​
searchDocs.content: </> interface TextFormatter { TextObject: TextObject-- Text object associated with the formatter. Text: string-- Current text of the textobject. BaseText: string-- Original text before being processed. Contexts: {[string]: boolean}-- Active context flags for triggering updates when a condition is met. (eg. input changes result in updates) ShouldAutoUpdate: boolean?-- Whether the formatter should be marked as being autoupdated each frame. Only change in callbacks. IsAutoUpdating: boolean?-- Whether the formatter is being auto-updated every frame. Do not manually change. Connections: {[any]: RBXScriptConnection } UpdateText: ( forceupdate: boolean?, overridetext: string?, isautoupdate: boolean? ) → () } This extends BaseFormatter and contains all its members.

searchDocs.title: AllFormatters​
searchDocs.content: </> MarkuaRbx.AllFormatters: {[TextObject]: TextFormatter} Dictionary mapping text objects to their associated formatter.

searchDocs.title: AutoUpdatingFormatters​
searchDocs.content: </> MarkuaRbx.AutoUpdatingFormatters: {[TextFormatter]: boolean} Dictionary containing all formatters marked as auto-updating.

searchDocs.title: FormattersByContext​
searchDocs.content: </> MarkuaRbx.FormattersByContext: {[string]: { [TextFormatter]: any, n: number }} Dictionary mapping context keys to formatters & their values. 'n' is number of formatters.

searchDocs.title: BindFormatter​
searchDocs.content: </> MarkuaRbx.BindFormatter(textobject: TextObject) → TextFormatter Assigns a TextFormatter to the provided textobject that processes tags everytime the textobject's text is changed.

searchDocs.title: UnbindFormatter​
searchDocs.content: </> MarkuaRbx.UnbindFormatter(textobject: TextObject) → () Removes the formatter associated with the provided textobject.

searchDocs.title: SetText​
searchDocs.content: </> MarkuaRbx.SetText( textobject: TextObject, text: string ) → () Updates the text for the provided textobject. If a formatter is associated with it, directly updates the text via it rather than firing the text changed signal.

searchDocs.title: GetFormattersByContext​
searchDocs.content: </> MarkuaRbx.GetFormattersByContext(keys: ...string) → {[TextFormatter]: boolean} Returns a dictionary of formatters associated with the provided context key(s).

searchDocs.title: StartListeners​
searchDocs.content: </> MarkuaRbx.StartListeners( tagOverride: string?-- Optional override for the tag used in CollectionService to find the text objects to format. ) → () Starts listening for text objects tagged with tagOverride or "TextFormatted" and automatically adds/removes formatters for them

searchDocs.title: BaseFormatter​
searchDocs.content: </> interface BaseFormatter { IsStatic: boolean-- Whether this formatter instance is static. Only true for formatter used in ProcessText() CacheEnabled: boolean?-- Whether format results should be stored in a cache UseCache: boolean?-- Whether the cached format results should be used. }

searchDocs.title: TagCallback​
searchDocs.content: </> type TagCallback = ( formatter: BaseFormatter, attr: string, innerText: string?, processInner: (string) → string ) → ( string, boolean? ) Called whenever the tag is processed inside a string. Should return replacement string and an optional boolean (true if the output cannot be cached).

searchDocs.title: CreateFormatter​
searchDocs.content: </> Markua.CreateFormatter() → BaseFormatter Creates a new formatter object.

searchDocs.title: RegisterTag​
searchDocs.content: </> Markua.RegisterTag( tagName: string,-- The identifier of the tag (eg. "color" for <color>). isVoid: boolean?,-- If true, the tag is processed as a void tag (<tag />), and innerText will not be passed to the callback. callback: TagCallback ) → () Registers a custom tag. Callback should return new text, and true if the text cannot be cached.

searchDocs.title: RemoveTag​
searchDocs.content: </> Markua.RemoveTag(tagName: string) → () Removes a previously registered tag by its name.

searchDocs.title: FormatText​
searchDocs.content: </> Markua.FormatText( formatter: BaseFormatter, text: string ) → string Formats the provided string using the provided formatter object.

searchDocs.title: ProcessText​
searchDocs.content: </> Markua.ProcessText(text: string) → string Formats the provided string without the need for a formatter object.

searchDocs.title: ParseAttrValue​
searchDocs.content: </> Markua.ParseAttrValue(value: string) → string | number | boolean Parses the provided value into a boolean, number, or string. If the value is not a valid boolean or number, it will be returned as a string.

searchDocs.title: ParseAttrDict​
searchDocs.content: </> Markua.ParseAttrDict( attr: string-- The raw attribute string formatted as key-value pairs (eg. a=123 b="hello"). ) → ( {[string]: any}?,-- A dictionary of parsed keys and values, or nil if syntax is malformed. string?-- An error message if attribute parsing failed. ) Parses the provided attribute string into a dictionary.

searchDocs.title: ParseAttrArray​
searchDocs.content: </> Markua.ParseAttrArray( attr: string-- The raw attribute string formatted as space-separated values (eg. 123 "string with spaces" true). ) → ( {any}?,-- An array of parsed attribute values, or nil if syntax is malformed. string?-- An error message if attribute parsing failed. ) Parses the provided attribute string into an array.

searchDocs.title: Binding TextLabels​
searchDocs.content: To attach Markua formatting directly to a TextLabel, TextBox, or TextButton, use BindFormatter:  local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local Markua = require(ReplicatedStorage.Markua) local LocalPlayer = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer local textLabel = script.Parent.TextLabel local formatter = Markua.BindFormatter(textLabel) textLabel.Text = `Welcome back, <pid {LocalPlayer.UserId}/>!` -- "Welcome back, <font color="#b74cff">anexpia</font>!"   To unbind and restore the original text:  Markua.UnbindFormatter(textLabel)

searchDocs.title: Setting Text Directly​
searchDocs.content: If you want to update text directly through an existing formatter without setting TextLabel.Text:  Markua.SetText(textLabel, "<fancytext>Hello World!</fancytext>") -- I don't feel like writing an example of how this would look, but you can imagine.   This is faster because text will only have to be changed once, particularly when you are changing it each frame.

searchDocs.title: Automatic Listeners​
searchDocs.content: Markua can automatically manage formatting text objects tagged with TextFormatted or whichever other tag you provide. Simply call StartListeners when the client initializes.  Markua.StartListeners()   You can also specify a custom tag name:  Markua.StartListeners("MyCustomTag")

searchDocs.title: Dynamic Contexts & Auto-updating​
searchDocs.content: If you have tags that change value dynamically depending on certain conditions (such as player team, preferred input, or keybinds), you can flag what you want your formatter to update on by adding a key to formatter.Contexts and iterating over the formatters with specific contexts when needed using GetFormattersByContext.  You can also mark formatters as auto-updating in tag callbacks by setting formatter.ShouldAutoUpdate to true.

searchDocs.title: Keybinds Example​
searchDocs.content: If you have a tag that depends on the player's keybinds, You can add the keybind to the contexts and update every formatter with the keybind when it changes.  local Markua = require(path.to.Markua) local ControlsModule = require(path.to.your.controls.module) -- register a tag that displays the keybind for a certain action Markua.RegisterTag("kb", true, function(formatter, attr) local display = ControlsModule.GetDisplay(attr) if display then formatter.Contexts[`kb{attr}`] = true return display else return `Invalid Control {attr}` end end) -- update each formatter that has the keybind when the keybind changes ControlsModule.ControlsChanged:Connect(function(controlname: string) local formatters = Markua.GetFormattersByContext(`kb{controlname}`) for formatter in formatters do formatter.UpdateText(true) end end)

searchDocs.title: Auto-updating Example​
searchDocs.content: local Markua = require(path.to.Markua) Markua.RegisterTag("timeuntil", true, function(formatter, attr, _, _) formatter.ShouldAutoUpdate = true -- marking this formatter as autoupdating. local start = tonumber(attr) if start then return tostring(math.round((workspace:GetServerTimeNow() - start) * 10) / 10), true -- returning true to indicate this doesn't cache. else return `Invalid Time {attr}` end end)

searchDocs.title: Registering Tags​
searchDocs.content: You can define custom tags using Markua.RegisterTag. Tag callbacks receive four arguments:  formatter: The current Formatter object.attr: The raw attribute string provided inside the tag.innerText: The content inside <tag>...</tag> (or nil for void tags).processInner: A helper function to recursively format innerText.

searchDocs.title: Standard Tag Example​
searchDocs.content: local symbols = {"!", "@", "#", "$", "%", "^", "&", "*", "?", "~"} Markua.RegisterTag("wackify", false, function(formatter, attr, innerText, processInner) local text = processInner(innerText) local result = "" -- randomly add symbols that replace characters or are added afterwards. for i = 1, #text do local char = string.sub(text, i, i) if math.random() < 0.3 then result ..= symbols[math.random(1, #symbols)] elseif math.random() < 0.3 then result ..= char .. symbols[math.random(1, #symbols)] else result ..= char end end -- return true as the second value to mark this as not cacheable. the result always changes. return result, true end) Markua.RegisterTag("uppercase", false, function(formatter, attr, innerText, processInner) return string.upper(processInner(innerText)) end) print(Markua.ProcessText("<uppercase><wackify>What is happening to me</wackify></uppercase>"))

searchDocs.title: Void Tag Example​
searchDocs.content: If a tag has no inner content (written as <tag />), set isVoid to true:   Markua.RegisterTag("currentobjective", true, function(formatter, attr, innerText, processInner) return Objectives.GetCurrentObjective() end) local text = Markua.ProcessText("Your current objective is <currentobjective />")

searchDocs.title: Basic Formatting​
searchDocs.content: For situations where caching isn't needed, such as processing tags once or only updating when needed, use Markua.ProcessText.  local Markua = require(path.to.Markua) local formatted = Markua.ProcessText("Hello <b>world</b>!") print(formatted)   If you have tags that dynamically change value even if the text itself doesn't, it is best to couple the text with a custom formatter. This allows you to cache the result of static tags and only update dynamic tags when needed.  Formatter.CacheEnabled enables or disables the cache. Formatter.UseCache controls whether the cache is read while processing text.  You should either disable Formatter.UseCache or clear Formatter.FormatCache when the text is changed or needs to be fully updated.  local UIS = game:GetService("UserInputService") local Markua = require(path.to.Markua) -- assume we have a textlabel on screen and referenced by 'textlabel' variable local attrToInput = { touch = Enum.PreferredInput.Touch, gamepad = Enum.PreferredInput.Gamepad, mouse = Enum.PreferredInput.KeyboardAndMouse, } Markua.RegisterTag("inputcontext", false, function(formatter, attr, innerText, processInner) local targetinput = attrToInput[attr] if not targetinput then return `Invalid input type {attr}` elseif UIS.PreferredInput == targetinput then return processInner(innerText) else return "" end end) Markua.RegisterTag("timesince", true, function(formatter, attr, _, processInner) local n = tonumber(attr) if n then return tostring((math.round((tick() - n) * 10) / 10)), true -- returning true to indicate this doesn't cache. else return `Invalid Time {attr}` end end) local formatter = Markua.CreateFormatter() formatter.CacheEnabled = true formatter.UseCache = true local template = `It has been <timesince {tick()}/> since this started.\ <inputcontext mouse>This text only appears if mouse is preferred input.</inputcontext>\ <inputcontext touch>This text only appears if touch is preferred input.</inputcontext>\ <inputcontext gamepad>This text only appears if gamepad is preferred input.</inputcontext>` UIS:GetPropertyChangedSignal("PreferredInput"):Connect(function() -- clear the cache, so that inputcontext tag is re-evaluated. table.clear(formatter.FormatCache) end) while task.wait() do -- constantly update the displayed text, only <timesince /> will be getting updated unless preferredinput changes. textlabel.Text = Markua.FormatText(formatter, template) end   The Roblox integration of Markua is a better example of how this is used.

searchDocs.title: Parsing Attributes​
searchDocs.content: Markua provides functions to decode attribute strings into dictionaries or arrays. Each returns a table or an error message if the attributes are malformed.  You can directly use the attribute string if you don't want to use them. This is the recommended way if you aren't adding multiple attributes for your tags.

searchDocs.title: Dictionaries (ParseAttrDict)​
searchDocs.content: local dict, err = Markua.ParseAttrDict('speed=15 active=true name="Player"') if dict then print(dict.speed) -- 15 (number) print(dict.active) -- true (boolean) print(dict.name) -- "Player" (string) without the quotes else error(err) end

searchDocs.title: Arrays (ParseAttrArray)​
searchDocs.content: local arr, err = Markua.ParseAttrArray('100 250 false "Hello World"') if arr then print(arr[1], arr[2], arr[3], arr[4]) -- 100 (number), 250 (number), false (boolean), "Hello World" (string) else error(err) end
